P1.evidence: Frame delivered in full — 'where we're at today, where we want to go, I we covered some of that already. What's been getting in the way, what we genuinely need to get there' — and agreement taken: 'That all sound good to you? Yeah.' Open question asked well and with a why-now edge: 'What's the biggest reason you're potentially looking to start coaching right now, all of a sudden?' P1a partial: the rep gestures at prior knowledge ('I know we covered some of this as well') but reads nothing specific back, and the prospect separately reveals he never watched the pre-call videos he was sent, which was an opening to acknowledge and was not used.

P2.evidence: The weakest phase in the entire batch, on the prospect who needed it most. Age, height and weight were never asked — the prospect volunteered his age in the first minute and his height and weight unprompted at minute 47. The health-conditions question was asked once, in passing, and the answer was two hip replacements; the rep said 'Okay' and moved to training. Injuries, chronic pain and movement limitations were never asked as a question at all, so the AC joint surgeries, the shortened Achilles and the inability to run all arrived because the prospect volunteered them. Most striking, diet was never asked. This prospect named nutrition as his primary weakness at least three times — 'my weakness is nutrition', 'I don't have a format for my nutrition', 'I need help with that' — and was never once asked what he actually eats, which meant the nutrition pillar was later delivered with no knowledge of his intake beyond night eating. Sleep and energy were also never asked, despite 'I struggle to sleep' being said twice. P2e is the one clear hit: 'typical training week, what's a normal training week look like?'. P2b partial — occupation was explored as rapport at minute 24, not as an activity question. This phase is the root cause of most of what follows.

P3.evidence: Reached real depth, but largely because the prospect is extraordinarily forthcoming rather than because the script ran. P3d was asked properly — 'why is all this stuff so important?... if we really had to summarize it, what's like the main motivation behind all of this for you?' — and the rep then ran a good sweep for P3b: 'mental health, sleep, relationships, being a role model, better dad, what are some of the other things just so we can get the checklist up?'. The best question on the call is the P3g driver: 'I look at my dad, my dad passed when he was 73 and in his 60s he was just comfortable. And most guys in their 60s I talk to, they're just comfortable. But you have a sense of drive to be better. What do you feel like behind that for you?' That produced identity, adversity and mortality material. P3a partial: physique goals surfaced from the prospect, not from the aesthetics question. P3c never asked, which is a real loss given he cannot run or play basketball. P3h is a miss and an expensive one — the prospect handed over 'we're in the death zone', 'I'm in the final quarter', a cholesterol scare, two daughters and a wedding, and none of it was ever reflected back to him.

P4.evidence: Effectively absent. What has he tried before, what happened with it and why it did not stick were all never asked. P4d and P4e get partial credit only because the prospect answered them unprompted inside his response to the opening question — 'I want to go to a level that I can't go to on my own... it's not easy on your own. You know, I'm a loner' — and later diagnosed his own failure mode precisely: 'I'll go like eight minutes. And then I finally start falling off, check my phone.' That is the gap, stated by the prospect, and it was never explored. P4f is a straightforward miss: the prospect literally framed the entire call as needing help doing it alone, and was never asked why he cannot. Note also that the tirzepatide is the most important past-attempt fact on the call — it is doing the work he is about to try to do without it — and no question was asked about what happens when he stops.

P5.evidence: Fourth consecutive sales call in this batch with no consequence frame. The two-year question was never asked, nor willing-to-settle, nor why-not. P5d was attempted and immediately conceded: 'Do you feel like it is kind of time to draw a line in this hand and really get this thing handled or like, how are you feeling right now?' drew a polite refusal — 'I mean, I feel good. I feel like I'm on, I'm not flattened out. I'm still on this path, right, by myself' — and the rep accepted it and moved on. This is the most conspicuous P5 omission of the nine calls because the prospect supplied every component himself and unprompted: a cholesterol of 240 four months ago, a refusal of statins that leaves lifestyle as the only lever, an imminent discontinuation of the drug currently controlling his eating, 'we're in the death zone as we move into our 60s', and 'I'm in the final quarter'. A single 'so what does that look like in two years if nothing changes?' had all of that behind it and was never asked.

P6.evidence: P6a asked cleanly: 'if we had all those dialed in for you, that's everything that you would need to get into the best shape of your life?' — answered with a qualification about having been a college soccer player and then 'I would say I'll be in the top 1% for 63-year-olds.' Credit to the rep for using the 1-to-10 instrument twice, before and after the delivery walkthrough, which is good practice and is worth propagating. But P6b was never asked in any form, and P6c is a clear miss: the score was an eight both times and the prospect stated explicitly why it could not be higher — 'until I'm doing it, I can't give the 10... the girl looks like an eight, but man, until you open up the package, you don't know.' That is unresolved hesitation, the script says return to Phase 5, and the rep went to price instead.

P11.evidence: Close attempted — 'it is sounding like that's not, we're not, I'm kind of getting the sense that we're still not feeling good 100%. Let's rock and roll with that right now' — and declined. No payment, so steps two to four unreachable. Worth recording that the fallback was weaker than the opportunity warranted: the prospect had just named the exact tier he wanted and written the figure down, and no deposit was requested, no onboarding slot was held, and no follow-up call was booked. The next step is an undated text.

objection_plays.detail: The first clean run of a scripted play anywhere in this batch. Trigger: 'There's still a little bit of hesitation' and 'seeing is believing. Implementing is believing.' The PLANE move ran close to verbatim — 'if you're up in the clouds, and you're looking down, there's always going to be a level of like nervousness, like, is this the holy crap, am I doing the right thing?' — and was then extended correctly to the deferral itself: 'we can go and land the plane and kind of fly back up tomorrow, but it doesn't really make that moment of decision any different if we come up the second day.' He also improvised a bar variant about approaching an attractive woman, which was well judged for this prospect and landed. What did not run: 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?', which was the exact diagnosis and was never named; the pleasure-versus-pain question; the BRIDGE; and the closing 'how will you know if you never actually try?'. The play was run and then not finished — the rep pivoted to price architecture rather than completing the sequence.

Trigger: 'it's a lot of money for me. You know, I'm retired.' The isolate and the ability-versus-uncertainty diagnostic both ran and both ran well — 'it's not like a logistical and like affordability thing. Like, if we wanted to do it for sure, like, it sounds like we have the money. It's just more a bit of an uncertainty thing at this point. Is that kind of where we're at?' — and the rep added a strong value-projection question about looking back after six months. Then nothing. Not one of the six financial-picture questions was asked, even though the prospect had volunteered 'I live off of seven to nine grand a month' and that the money would come out of savings, which is precisely the moment the script exists for. The break-it-up conversation, when it finally came, was mishandled in the other direction: asked directly whether payment plans existed, the rep said most people pay by credit card, and only disclosed ten minutes later that plans exist with a surcharge.

Triggered clearly and more than once — 'I always take my time to internalize it', 'it is something that I am going to contemplate and think about for a minute', 'I'm not just going to be like, here's my credit card this moment.' No OA move ran. The rep answered a deliberation objection with the fear play and then with a cheaper tier, neither of which addresses deliberation. Notably 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?' was never asked, and it would have been productive: the prospect had already given the answer twice, that he cannot evaluate the programme without being inside it, which is exactly what the love-it-or-leave-it solves and which the rep never explicitly connected.

A distinct objection with no scripted play: the prospect wants a monthly subscription, not a term commitment, and said so plainly — 'If it were a monthly thing, and I was seeing the progress, and you guys were like, this is how much it is a month. I'd be like, all right, well, let's rock this thing for a couple months and see how I do.' Also unaddressed and related: 'my only concern is very systemized, which is good, but it's digital. It's distance. It's from a distance. It's you plug me into a system with the other people.' That is a delivery-model objection from a prospect who has just been told the live coaching is group rather than one-to-one, and it received no response at all before the rep moved to the trial offer.

notes: A prospect who wanted to buy, said so, named the tier and wrote the price down, on a call that skipped almost the entire baseline. Diet, sleep, energy, injuries, height and weight were never asked of a 62-year-old with two hip replacements, a cholesterol scare, and an active GLP-1 prescription he plans to stop. Three coaching actions. First, P2 is not optional and it is least optional on older prospects — the nutrition pillar was delivered to a man whose diet had never been discussed. Second, P5: the cost of inaction was handed over unprompted on this call in the prospect's own words and was never used. Third, when a prospect asks whether payment plans exist, answer accurately the first time; saying 'most people just put it on a credit card' and then disclosing ten minutes later that plans exist with a surcharge is the single most damaging thing said on this recording. Worth propagating from this call: the double 1-to-10 check either side of the delivery walkthrough, and the plane play, which is the first properly executed scripted objection play in the batch.
